new.description: the 0.19 series a consumer takes: the ledger cutover and the plan-state split

the listing, the per-file reads, the tip read file by file, the ship's `git rm`
the resolved directory through the legs
the queue's fence glob, and the legacy file riding planArtifacts so a plan tick can `git rm` it
the package's read of the queue
the queue's name where it is spelled
the listing, the reads and the ship
the fence glob and the legacy allowance

summary: `Chain.pendingDir` replaces `Chain.pendingPath`: the ledger is a directory of `<tag>.json`, its own `*.json` is the listing, and a ship `git rm`s exactly what shipped

per.section: The ledger is a directory — one entry per file

acceptance: Every queue read and the ship resolve `Chain.pendingDir`; a `*.json` directly under it is an entry and a subdirectory is not walked; a file whose `tag` disagrees with its filename is refused naming both; `flume status` and `flume check` read the directory; `docs/MIGRATING-0.19.md` carries the series' breaking changes, the plan-state split among them.
tests: a *.json directly under the pending directory is an entry and a subdirectory is not walked
an entry file whose tag disagrees with its filename is refused naming both
a parse failure names the entry file it read
a ship removes exactly the shipped entries' files and edits no other entry
flume status reports pending: unparsable when one entry file is malformed
pins: an absent pending directory reads as nothing pending
notes: Tag uniqueness becomes the filesystem's, so the composed list schema's duplicate issue goes. This repo's own live queue is an operator cutover — `.flume/` is outside every phase's fence — and the legacy file rides planArtifacts so a plan tick can `git rm` it. MIGRATING-0.19 is the series page: it also owes the plan-state split (b6f882c3) and `PLAN_STATE_PATH` leaving `SHARED_PROMPT_DATA_KEYS`.

edit.description: stake before provisioning, drop at ship or teardown
skip a claimed entry as a quarantined one is skipped
the claimed set on a producer's rendered block

summary: A build tick stakes `<git-common-dir>/flume/claims/<slug>` before provisioning and drops it when the attempt ends; selection skips a claimed entry

per.section: Claims — an entry in flight is left alone

acceptance: A claim exists from before its entry's worktree is provisioned until the attempt ends, with the ship or the teardown; `TickContext.claimed` and `TickResult.claimedTags` report the set the tick read; selection skips a claimed entry and a claim held by a dead pid is reclaimed.
tests: a build tick stakes its entry's claim before provisioning the worktree
the claim is removed when an attempt ends without shipping
selection skips an entry another tick holds a claim on
TickResult.claimedTags reports the claims the tick read
a claim held by a dead pid is reclaimed by the next selection
notes: Reported, never inferred: nothing outside the engine re-reads the claims directory. What a producer does about a claimed entry it would have changed stays the chain's.

edit.description: the third check, and `opts.hint` over all three
wire it afterMerge on the producer phases

summary: pendingGate's third check: a gated commit leaves a claimed entry's file byte-identical, or is refused naming the entry and its holder

per.section: `pendingGate` — validation and fence pre-check as an opt-in builtin

acceptance: A commit that edits or removes a claimed entry's file fails pendingGate naming the entry and the holding pid; an edit to an unclaimed entry passes; the check runs afterMerge over the merged tree and `opts.hint` appends to its message as to the other two.
tests: pendingGate refuses a commit that edits a claimed entry's file, naming the entry and the holder
pendingGate refuses a commit that removes a claimed entry's file
pendingGate passes a commit that edits an unclaimed entry
opts.hint appends to the claim-check violation message
notes: afterMerge because a pre-merge read passes over exactly the tree the collision is not in; uncontended under one producer. It is the section's only merged-tree gate: there is no duplicate refusal beside it — the drain folds a duplicate instead (THE-DRAIN-FOLDS-A-DUPLICATE-FINDING).

edit.description: re-read the store after the tick's work, onto the handoff result
`refusedForPlan` reads the reported set, not the no-commit tables
the window/handoff agreement pin, now over one evidence
the field a handoff may read

summary: `TickResult` reports the standing prior-attempt records, so a handoff reads the refusal set instead of rebuilding it from no-commit and merge modes

per.section: A fact the engine holds is reported, never rediscovered

acceptance: `TickResult` carries the prior-attempt store as the tick left it; `refusedForPlan` (`harness/handoff.ts`) decides off that set rather than off `PLAN_RESOLVES_NO_COMMIT`/`PLAN_RESOLVES_MERGE`; the inbox window and the handoff read one evidence, so the two-table agreement they were kept in by hand has no second side.
tests: TickResult carries the standing prior-attempt records as the tick left them
the default handoff routes a walled entry to the inbox off the reported record set
notes: `TickContext.priorAttempts` already reports the set at tick start (`src/Dispatcher.ts`); the handoff runs after and has no such field, which is why the package reconstructs it from modes. Reported as a fact — what a chain does about a standing refusal stays the chain's (`engine-boundary.md`). The store is written mid-tick, so the handoff's copy is a fresh `readAll()`, not the tick-start one.

new.description: the wave's merge/gate/revert/ledger stage: takes the per-entry results, answers the merge outcomes and gate rows the verdict needs

edit.description: `runFanout` calls the stage; the ship lock's span becomes a signature, not a brace pair

summary: Split `runFanout`'s merge stage — the ~500-line try from the cherry-pick loop to `clearMergingMarkers` — out of `src/waveTick.ts` into its own module
acceptance: `src/waveTick.ts` holds the wave's provisioning and agent fanout; the merge stage is a named function in its own file, taking the per-entry results and answering the merge outcomes and gate rows. Behavior-free: tsc, the default lane, and the export and citation pins hold it.
notes: Observed by the tick that shipped SIBLING-TICKS-TAKE-TURNS-AT-GIT: after the ship lock landed, the stage is one `try` whose only marker is an indent level (src/waveTick.ts is 1234 lines). No behavior moves — a split that changes an outcome is the wrong split.

edit.description: `phases: [build, ...planSlices]`; the list's narration names budget priority, and the ladder stays `nextPhase`'s

summary: The cascade example declares build ahead of its plan slices, and says the phase list is budget priority — its cascade lives in `nextPhase`, not in the list
acceptance: `examples/cascade-chain.ts` returns `phases: [build, ...planSlices]`, and the prose at the list names it as the budget's priority (`spec/harness.md`, *The phases*) distinct from the dependency ladder `nextPhase` holds. `tests/examples.test.ts` pins the shipped order.
tests: the cascade example declares build first and its plan slices after it
notes: Decides nothing for the example itself — its ladder holds one flag at a time — but the list is public surface a chain author copies, and copied into a chain with no ladder it inverts the loop's economics at the default budget of one. The `Ladder order is dependency order` comment stays true of `nextPhase` and must not be moved onto the list.
